thread:
sasha: Quick heads-up — I ran a co-residency experiment packing 2 medium LLMs + 1 small reranker on a single A100 80GB and hit intermittent OOMs after we bumped kernel selection heuristics yesterday. Root cause not obvious yet.

mike: Can you paste the perf dump and allocator stats? Might be wasted workspace or fragmentation.

sasha: Paste below. This is from the runtime profiler (shortened):
```
TIMESTAMP=1755004310
models: [gpt-medium:v2, gpt-medium:v1, rerank-small:v1]
kernel_policy: auto_select_priority=[faster-kernels, fuse-attn]
batch_window=20ms
allocator: pool_total=78000MB pool_free=3200MB largest_free_block=1.2GB
kv_cache: resident=14GB pinned_pages=0
OOM_event: worker-3 alloc(2.4GB) failed at 0x7f8b...
````

ana: Noted. Two quick hypotheses: 1) kernel changes increased transient workspace per-layer (esp fused kernels use more temp buffers). 2) our allocator fragmentation increased because we do lazy free of KV pages when model swap happens.

kai: Replied to the perf-bot alert? perf-bot: "regression: p99 token latency +12% after kernel change on co-residency runs".

perf-bot: regression detected for /generate endpoint across co-residency tests. See perf link: https://perf.internal/runs/1755

mike: I ran a microbenchmark toggling kernel_policy. With `fuse-attn` on, steady-state mem high-water increased by ~3.8GB vs baseline. Also observed 6% lower throughput but +8% p99. So fused kernels not win for these mixed-model footprints.

sasha: OK interesting. Also KV cache behavior: when second medium model loads, we lazily copy its KV to GPU on first request, but we pre-alloc a page table entry. That plus per-kernel workspace spikes looks like pushes us past fragmentation threshold.

ana: Suggests two possible fixes: 1) allocator tuning: reserve a contiguous workspace slab for transient kernel buffers (workspace_slab_size per model) so kernels can use that instead of scattering allocations. 2) model slotting: enforce fixed VRAM partitions per model class to avoid interleaved fragmentation.

mike: Quick config prototype I tried (yaml):
```yaml
runtime:
  allocator:
    mode: slab 
    slab_size_mb: 4096  # per-model transient workspace
    reuse_policy: LRU
  kv_cache:
    lazy_load: true
    eviction_threshold_mb: 2048
  co_residency:
    partitions:
      - class: medium
        min_reserve_mb: 22000
      - class: small
        min_reserve_mb: 6000
```

sasha: With slab mode + 4GB per-medium we saw no OOMs in 30m soak and p99 improved back to baseline. Throughput slightly down (~2%) but stable.

kai: Solid. Downside is wasted reserved memory in low-util periods. Could we support dynamic slab reclamation? E.g., mark slabs as reclaimable if idle > Xs and have a fast defragmentation path to coalesce.

ana: We can implement a two-tier allocator: owned slabs (per-model, fast path) + shared pool (fallback). Owned slabs are try-first; shared pool uses best-fit with occasional compacting passes. Also implement fast free-list for per-kernel temps to avoid malloc/free hotspots.

mike: Another mitigation: limit kernel policy to not choose fused kernels when free_contiguous < 8GB. Cheap guard prevents high workspace kernels from being selected. Pseudocode: `if (kernel.workspace_req > free_contig_threshold) skip_fused`.

sasha: Good. We should also adjust KV cache behavior: prefer streaming KV pages from CPU to GPU for cold models rather than allocating upfront. Use async prefetch when upcoming tokens predicted.

perf-bot: note: schedule regression re-run with slab allocator on co-residency test matrix (job 1755-rc2).

ana: Action items: 1) mike to land kernel selection guard + bench (ETA 2d). 2) sasha to prototype slab allocator config and run 2h soak (ETA 3d). 3) kai to design partitioning + reclamation spec (ETA EOD Friday). 4) perf-bot will run matrix.

mike: I'll attach microbench results after lunch.

sasha: Thanks. If anyone wants to reproduce quick: run `./tools/co_residency_bench --models gpt-medium:gpt-medium:rerank-small --tokens 50000 --kernel-policy auto` and watch `runtime/allocator/stats`.

kai: Adding note: this impacts Dedicated plans where we guarantee isolation; any reservation scheme must respect tenant SLAs.

ana: Agreed. We'll add telemetry for slab usage, fragmentation ratio, and KV_page_faults to the console dashboard so customers can see tradeoffs.

mike: (thumbsup)

sasha: Closing loop: initial fix path = kernel guard + slab allocator prototype. Will sync in tomorrow engineering standup.
